title: Unused locals r, g, h in two health tests
detail: Bound in test_health_hysteresis_band_and_enter and again at line 405 in test_health_drain_max_not_sum_e16, never referenced afterward. Odin rejects unused local declarations, so the test package will not build.
recommended_fix: Use `_, _, _ := health_narrow_fixture(...)` or actually use the returned node ids.

title: Grace-row count omitted when zero — frame ambiguous for reader
detail: When health_enabled and no grace rows are active, the count field is not written at all. A symmetric reader cannot tell whether rows follow meter_pct; the conditional presence makes the section unframeable.
recommended_fix: Always write the grace-row count (0 when empty) whenever health_enabled, so the section layout is fixed.

title: Zero-severity class suppresses Grace_Expired forever
detail: Validation allows health_drain_pct_per_tick == 0; with all severities 0, drain stays 0 and the expired-class loop never runs, so Grace_Expired is silently dropped — contradicting the header contract 'expiry while still breached emits Grace_Expired'.
recommended_fix: Emit Grace_Expired independent of drain, or validate per-class severity >= 1 like the cap.

title: 're-step-safe' claim contradicted by rolling-sum update
detail: On a same-tick re-step dd == 0, so the stored slot delta is SUBTRACTED from win_delivered and the slot zeroed — the rolling sums permanently undercount, contradicting the 're-step-safe' comments at lines 21 and 306 of health.odin.
recommended_fix: Guard the subtraction (skip when dd == 0) or drop the re-step-safe claim.

title: Tautological assertion — grace-cell pin can never fail
evidence:
+	testing.expectf(t, s.health.grace[0].grace_left > 0 || s.health.grace[0].grace_left == 0,
+		"grace cell present for email")
detail: grace_left > 0 || grace_left == 0 is true for every u32; the 'grace cell present' assertion adds zero verification value and cannot detect a wrong or missing grace cell.
recommended_fix: Assert len(s.health.grace) > 0 and a meaningful bound on grace_left (e.g., <= 400).

title: Exit margin above tolerance silently clamps exit threshold to zero
detail: Validation only requires margins >= 0. A margin >= a class's tolerance makes exit_loss 0, so the class exits only when the window holds zero loss and zero latency — stricter than 'meaningfully under its tolerance'.
recommended_fix: Validate margins below the smallest class tolerance, or clamp to tolerance - 1.

title: Decimal policy inconsistent: jint (balance) vs jint_strict (packet_types)
detail: Packet-types health fields use strict ints (a decimal rejects); the balance health block uses non-strict jint despite the ODN-10 integer-only comment — a decimal balance value is silently accepted.
recommended_fix: Use jint_strict for the balance health block and reject on parse failure.

title: Contradictory grace/drain numbers across drain-max test comments
evidence:
+	health_catalog_fast_grace(cat) // both classes' grace 50 (the streaming
+	// breach ~5 -> drains from ~55; the email breach ~95 -> drains from ~145)
+	step_n(&s, 410, cat) // streaming drains from ~405; email (grace 10) from ~100
+	cat.packet_types[0].health_grace_ticks = 300
detail: The fixture sets email grace to 300 (drains from ~390, band [404,~447]); this test claims grace 50, then 10, and band [~145,~204]. Three mutually contradictory timelines for the same run.
recommended_fix: Recompute and unify the comments (email grace 300; overlap ~405-455).

title: Fixture header claims breach ~260 ticks; tests assert ~5
evidence:
+// within ~260 ticks); the mult2 catalog variant (surge 2/tick — the 4.2
+	// the windowed loss breaches at ~tick 5 (Grace_Started).
detail: The header says the saturated fixture breaches 'within ~260 ticks'; several tests assert Grace_Started by ~5 and expiry ~405, and their assertions depend on the early timing. One of these is wrong.
recommended_fix: Confirm the actual breach tick and reconcile the header with the test comments.

title: Serialization pin byte-scan can false-match unrelated fields
evidence:
+		if dump[i] == 0x64 && dump[i+1] == 0x00 && dump[i+2] == 0x00 && dump[i+3] == 0x00 {
+			found_meter = true
detail: Any little-endian u32 equal to 100 anywhere in the dump (e.g., score) matches 64 00 00 00 — the pin passes even if the health section were absent, so it cannot catch a serialization regression.
recommended_fix: Parse the dump structurally or use a unique marker instead of a raw byte scan.

title: recharge 0 (valid) emits no-op Meter_Changed every healthy tick
evidence:
+	} else if !any_breach && h.meter_pct < 100 {
+		event_emit_meter(state, tick, h.meter_pct)
detail: Validation allows recharge_pct_per_tick == 0; with a drained-but-healthy meter the branch still emits Meter_Changed with an unchanged value every tick, contradicting the tag comment 'the health meter moved'.
recommended_fix: Skip the emission when recharge == 0, or validate recharge >= 1.

title: prev_in_surge unsaved — mid-surge restore discards accumulated uptime
evidence:
+	if in_surge && !h.prev_in_surge {
+		h.surge_delivered = 0 // a NEW surge starts a fresh window (never double-count)
+			w_bool(&w, h.surge_done)
+	prev_in_surge:   bool, // derived — the deactivation-edge detector
detail: prev_in_surge is 'derived' and not serialized; a state restored mid-surge sees in_surge && !prev_in_surge and zeroes the restored accumulators, changing the win ratio versus continuous play.
recommended_fix: Serialize prev_in_surge, or reconstruct it on load from surge_active.
